chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: How his friendship with Basie developed in Chicago
summary: Basie's band left the Grand Terrace in slow winters, came to the DeLisa breakfast shows, and Saunders got close to Jo Jones.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Great people. Speaking of stride piano players, Basie's good in stride.
But he's from the old school.
He's from the old school. You catch him in that boom-boom, boom-boom.
You said you first met Basie in Kansas City.
And evidently, through the years your paths have crossed and I would imagine you're pretty good friends, playing at your 50th anniversary.
How did that develop? Say, when the band came here from Kansas City in -- what was it, '36?

Yeah, well, see, I had met him in Kansas City before that. And they had a habit at the Grand Terrace when business was bad, like, this winter, we had -- Fox would sent everybody home. But Mike DeLisa, he never did, he kept his doors open regardless is it was one person in there or two or 100.
So -- and then Basie and them, they was -- on bad nights he'd let everybody go home. And so --
That's right, they came up here in the winter.

Right, and do they would come over and they would come to the breakfast shows and all of that. And then this is when I really met and got close with Jo Jones, because Jo -- I don't know, he took a liking to me and he used to come around all the time. So did Sid, the last days, when he -- well, we had been friends down through the years, but not where he was always like in New York or somewhere like that. And then the last years -- I mean, the last year or two, he was here at the -- with Bill Rinehart at the Jazz Limited.
